questions.stem: Why are metals good conductors of electricity?

options.text: They contain delocalised electrons that are free to move and carry charge

questions.explanation: Metals have metallic bonding, where outer electrons are delocalised (free to move) through the structure. These free electrons can carry electrical charge when a voltage is applied. Most non-metals lack free electrons, so they are poor conductors.

questions.stem: What type of oxide do non-metals typically form?
questions.explanation: Non-metals typically form acidic oxides. For example, CO₂ dissolves in water to form carbonic acid (H₂CO₃), and SO₂ forms sulfurous acid (H₂SO₃). In contrast, metal oxides are typically basic and can neutralise acids.
